sam: Heads-up: model-bridge candidate 'bridge-7b-int3' landed on staging. Quick snapshot: perplexity up on long-doc suite and we observed inconsistent list formatting + some invented identifiers in answers. I uploaded 54 flagged prompts: s3://staging/bridge/fails/4123456789/flags.json. Looping in @elaine for dedupe and @rob for quant triage.

elaine: grabbing the file now. First pass: ~20% of these look like duplicate scrapes and ~10% look like HTML-encoded inputs. Which tokenizer was used for ingest?

rob: ran a focused quant-smoke on int3 artifact. Observed a bump in hallucination-like tokens when seq>2000; also noticed matmul kernel fallback warnings on older driver images. Snippet: ```
quant-smoke: model=bridge-7b-int3
longform_fail_rate=0.039
issue_summary=hallucination_spike+format_truncate at seq>2000
gpu_warn=matmul-fallback v5.2 drivers
```

label-bot: Fail list + minimal manifest uploaded: s3://staging/bridge/manifest_4123456789.csv (fields: prompt_id, md5, tokenhash_v3, embed512). ACL: eng-ml-read.

sam: ingest used tokenizer v3. My proposal: create ephemeral golden set name "bridge-longform-regress-4123" target 220 items (120 hallucination/consistency, 100 format/truncation). Dedupe against master-golden-v3 using tokenhash_v3 exact + embed cosine clustering. @elaine can you run dedupe with these rules?

elaine: Sounds good. Dedupe rules I'm using: 1) html-unescape + normalize whitespace; 2) exact tokenhash_v3 => drop; 3) embed512 cosine >= 0.90 => cluster and keep exemplar; 4) for near-paraphrases (0.85-0.90) surface for manual review. Kicking off now.

rob: short-term mitigation: I'll add a routing rule that sends requests with estimated_output_tokens>1900 to bridge-q4b-compat. Canary 8% for 6h. Also opened ticket INF-9123 for kernel fallback.

label-bot: Dedupe finished: 16 exact tokenhash_v3 drops, 9 near-dup clusters merged (exemplars kept). After augmenting with 200 sampled long-docs stratified by source, candidate pool = 239. Wrote candidates to s3://staging/bridge/golden_candidates_4123456789.json and manifest to s3://staging/bridge/golden_candidates_4123456789.csv.

sam: Nice. For labeling ops we need a concise rubric and examples. Draft rubric points: HALLUCINATION (explicitly invented facts/entities), TRUNCATION (abrupt cutoff), FORMAT (lists/tables corrupted), PARTIAL_OK (first N tokens accurate), ID_MISMATCH (generated ids not present). Examples: one each uploaded to s3://staging/bridge/rubric_examples_4123456789.md.

elaine: I also noticed some tokenhash_v3 collisions where the same md5 had different tokenhash due to whitespace normalization differences; I normalized and rehashed, noted collision_count=7 in manifest. Added cluster metadata (cluster_id, cluster_size) to help label ops.

rob: route-bot: routing rule applied: longform-temp-bridge -> bridge-q4b-compat (8% traffic) until 2026-03-27T12:00:00Z.

route-bot: Canary created and active.

ops-bot: For label ops: 239 items -> ~36-48h workload with 2 annotators + 1 QA. Please confirm start time once rubric + manifest final. Also ops opened a short-term dataset hold ticket DS-451 to prevent auto-harvest merges.

sam: I'll finish rubric and push final manifest by EOD. Plan to start labeling 2026-03-26T18:00:00Z PST. ETA first 50 labels ~14h. I'll run eval-harness after 50 and post metrics.

elaine: small note: I flagged 12 items with HTML vs plaintext ambiguity; labeled them as NEEDS_MANUAL_NORMALIZE in manifest so labelers know to preserve markup.

rob: monitoring canary metrics; if hallucination or truncation exceed baseline + 1 sigma we'll pause and rollback routing. Posting kernel ticket link to #eng-runtime.

sam: thanks team. I'll pull first eval and drop summary here. :thumbsup:
